q: Any increase in pressure at the surface of an enclosed fluid must be transmitted to ____ in the fluid.
e: This is the core concept of Pascal's law, describing the transmission of pressure in an incompressible fluid.

q: This concept was first recognized by French scientist ____ in 1650.
e: Blaise (or Balise, as written in the text) Pascal formulated this principle of fluid mechanics.

q: When a fluid completely fills a vessel and a pressure is applied to it at any part of the surface, that pressure is transmitted ____ throughout the whole of the enclosed fluid.
e: The applied pressure does not diminish as it travels through the enclosed fluid.
Pascal's law is the foundation for hydraulic systems.

q: The concept of Pascal's law is very useful in practice in the working principle of the ____ and hydraulic presses.
e: Hydraulic brakes use Pascal's law to multiply the force from the brake pedal to the brake pads.

q: A hydraulic press is used for baling jute, hay, cotton and also for the pressing of the ____ and for shaping steel and metal sheets.
e: Hydraulic presses provide the massive force required for industrial metal forming and compaction.
A hydraulic press allows a small input force to generate a much larger output force.

q: According to Pascal's law, the pressure $p_{in}$ is equal to the pressure ____ exerted on area $A_{out}$ of large piston.
e: The pressure is uniform throughout the enclosed fluid, so the pressure at the input piston equals the pressure at the output piston.

q: The upward force $F_{out}$ on area $A_{out}$ is $F_{out} =$ ____.
e: Since pressure is equal, the output force is the input pressure multiplied by the larger output area.

q: Assuming there is no friction in the hydraulic press system, the work done by effort equals the ____ done by the upward force.
e: This reflects the conservation of energy; the smaller force moves a greater distance to do the same amount of work as the larger force.

q: where $l_{in}$ = the distance travelled by ____ piston.
e: The input piston must travel a larger distance to displace enough fluid to move the large piston a small distance.
The output piston moves a smaller distance proportionally to the ratio of the areas.

q: Another useful machine based on Pascal's law is a ____ lift.
e: Hydraulic lifts use the same force multiplication principle to raise heavy loads like cars in a garage.

q: By applying a small force on the small piston produces a large upward force on the large piston which can lift a large ____.
e: The primary function of a hydraulic lift is to elevate heavy objects with minimal input effort.
